regime: Risk-On Reversal (Indexes Reclaim and Run, Gold Breaks to Fresh Highs, Crude Cracks)
summary: The election overhang cleared and the tape turned risk-on hard. The Nasdaq bought back a violent overnight washout to 27,611.50 and closed up 0.94 percent at 28,567.50, back above its 50-hour average, while the S&P added 1.65 percent to 7,721.75 and reclaimed both its stop and its EMA50. VIX collapsed about 19 percent to 16.71 as the fear bid drained out. Gold did not cool off, it ran another 3.63 percent to 4,074.30 and printed fresh highs above 4,000. The one board that broke was crude, down 8.10 percent to 88.71 on a clean stop break, so money left oil even as risk appetite came back everywhere else.

event.name: First session after US midterm Election Day; no confirmed tier-one US release (federal data shutdown-delayed)
event.consensus: Nov 3 was US midterm Election Day, with results arriving overnight. The federal data calendar stays thin and shutdown-contingent, so scheduled releases were not the driver. The marquee read is still the October jobs report, normally Friday Nov 6, shutdown-contingent.
event.actual: A sharp risk-on reversal. After a violent overnight washout, equities reclaimed and extended above their stops and 50-hour averages, VIX collapsed about 19 percent, and gold ran to fresh highs. Crude broke down hard.
event.surprise: The speed of the turn and the VIX collapse. The overnight flush to a 27,611.50 MNQ low was fully bought back, and crude fell 8.10 percent against an otherwise risk-on tape.
event.nqReaction: NQ round-tripped the overnight low at 27,611.50 and closed up 0.94 percent at 28,567.50, reclaiming its EMA50 at 28,445 and tagging the 28,500 round. An opening-range up-break at 14:45 UTC failed and it closed mid-range below NYVWAP 28,677.
event.crossAsset: MES plus 1.65 percent at 7,721.75, back above its stop and EMA50. December gold plus 3.63 percent at 4,074.30, fresh highs above 4,000. December crude minus 8.10 percent at 88.71, a clean stop break. VIX about 16.71, down roughly 19 percent.

observe.name: OBSERVE lane
observe.note: No OBSERVE-lane signals today. GAP_NQ and TSMOM252LO_NQ sit outside the Net Alpha Pro curriculum and are tracked for research only.

risk.sizing: Normal. The indexes reclaimed their stops and 50-hour averages and VIX collapsed to the mid-teens, so the reduced stance from the selloff can step back to normal size. But the overnight was violent and crude broke 8 percent, so honor the stops and do not oversize into gaps.
risk.openRisk: The index longs are above their stops and EMA50s, the healthiest setup in a week, but they are two-day reclaims that stalled just under the AVWAP, so they can still fail at resistance. Gold is extended after a 3.6 percent run and can mean-revert. Crude is in free-fall below its stop. The overnight session proved the tape can gap hard either way.
risk.note: Throttle state NORMAL, stepped up from REDUCED after both indexes reclaimed their stops and 50-hour averages and VIX collapsed about 19 percent to 16.71. No drawdown flags and the daily loss budget is unused. TSMOM is long the indexes above their rising stops (MNQ 28,301, MES 7,660) and long gold above 4,030, and short crude below 91.42. The long-only momentum edge (E3v2) gate flipped back to green with price above the EMA50 and ROC positive, so it is live again but early. Week ahead: weekly jobless claims land Thursday and the October jobs report is due Friday Nov 6, both shutdown-contingent; the next policy event is the December FOMC. Keep size disciplined after a violent overnight and a hard crude break.

psychology: Yesterday the lesson was that a reclaim is a pause, not a buy. Today the market answered. Both indexes did not just hold their reclaimed stops, they cleared the 50-hour average that had capped them. The hard part was the overnight. Price flushed to 27,611.50 before the cash session ripped it all back. If you anchored to that low and shorted the hole, the reversal ran you over. The read is simple and uncomfortable: once price reclaims the level that rejected it, the short thesis is done, and chasing the breakdown after the fact is how you give back the patience you earned. Let the close above the EMA50 confirm the turn, and if you are still leaning short out of habit, that is the bias to check.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html:
Wide opening range, failed up-break, mid-range close. OR High 28,809, OR Low 28,405, Width 404 pts.

Anchored at the 14:30 UTC NY cash open (EST, after daylight saving ended Nov 1). The open was violent: price ran from the 28,430.50 cash open to 28,809 inside the first 15 minutes, a wide 404 point range. Price poked above the range at 14:45 UTC to 28,852.75, a failed up-break, then chopped back inside and closed the 20:00 UTC cash-close bar at 28,567.50, mid-range and below NYVWAP 28,677.40. There was no down-break. Today is a Wednesday, so HOF and MID are filter-blocked; BIR and BNC are eligible. The failed up-break and the close back inside the range is the BIR structure. Volume is disclaimed on the continuous contract, so VWAP uses a typical-price mean.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html:
Gate GREEN, no fresh breakout signal. Price closed 28,567.50, above EMA(50) at 28,445, with ROC(12) at plus 0.76 percent, so the long-only gate flipped back to green after being blocked through the selloff.

RVOL is not available (volume disclaimed on the continuous contract). The regime filter reads green on the reclaim, so the E3v2 long-only edge is eligible again, but ROC is only mildly positive on a day-two repair rather than a fresh-high breakout, so treat it as an early, borderline read rather than a strong momentum regime.

Price drifted lower into the close and finished 28,567.50, right on the minus 2 sigma band at 28,564.22, about 1.9 sigma under the session mean. That reads like a stretched touch, but it came as a pullback into the close on a net up day rather than a capitulation flush and reclaim, so it is a borderline reversion setup rather than a clean one. A reversion-grade long would want a stretched touch of the minus 2 or minus 3 sigma band followed by a reclaim back toward the mean, which has not confirmed, so the reversion edge is borderline-out today.

yesterdaysMapScore.note: Published Nov 3 for the Wednesday Nov 4 session. The map hedged a capped bounce against a stop loss, and the market resolved up: four of five rows triggered, three playing out. The MNQ reclaim row delivered to a 28,970.75 high past the prior high, gold's long ran to fresh highs above 4,000, and crude's short collapsed 8.10 percent. The MNQ lose-the-stop row triggered overnight and tagged its downside targets but V-reversed and closed up, so it graded mixed. The one not-triggered row was the neutral boxed scenario, which never set up because price cleared the EMA50.
